about: The `report_anomalies` table, published whole. See /api/schema for its grain. This file is fy 2013 only.

rows.table: Summary of receipts by category
rows.detail: Labels present, values absent — identical failure to FY2011 and FY2012.

rows.table: General fund appropriations and expenditures, line by line, FY2013
rows.detail: THE TABLE HEADING AND THE COLUMN HEADER ROW ARE ENTIRELY ABSENT — the string 'PROGRAM NAME' does not occur anywhere in the FY2013 file, where it appears four times in FY2012. p65 starts mid-table at 'Selectmen's Salaries'.

rows.table: Special revenue funds: grants, gifts and revolving accounts, FY2013
rows.detail: The table heading and column headers are absent again (p71 starts at 'Conservation Fund'), but the opening balances tie exactly to FY2012's closing balances ($2,062,621.79 in both), which chains all three years' special revenue tables together.

rows.table: Salary Administration Plan step definitions (Article 27)
rows.detail: This is the mechanism behind step costs in the payroll, and the dollar values of the steps are not printed anywhere in the report.

The front-page fact block on p4 is a verbatim reprint of the FY2012 one and is stale in every field: it gives FY2012's valuation and the 2012 town census in the FY2013 report, and still names Scott P. Brown as US senator and John W. Olver as representative, both of whom had left office by then. The assessors' own table eight pages later gives a different valuation.

The Monty Tech section is printed twice: pp44-57 is the current year's submission and pp58-59 is a verbatim reprint of the FY2012 report's enrollment and awards pages. There is no October 2013 enrollment-by-member-town breakdown anywhere in the document.

rows.table: Town at a glance: population, valuation, tax rate and legislative delegation
rows.detail: THIS BLOCK IS A VERBATIM REPRINT OF THE FY2012 ONE and is stale: it gives the 2012 town census (9982), the FY2012 assessed valuation ($1,101,654,500 real estate, $29,375,244 personal property) and 'TAX RATE: $ 17.30 (Fiscal 2013)', while the assessors' own table on p10 gives FY2013 valuation as $1,131,029,744.

rows.table: Town department office hours
rows.detail: Identical to FY2012's, including the footer '(TOWN HALL, RITTER MEMORIAL BUILDING AND LUNENBURG PUBLIC LIBRARY AND EAGLE HOUSE CLOSED FRIDAY)' — the four-day week continued.

rows.table: Monty Tech enrollment, admissions and Class of 2012 awards (reprinted from the FY2012 report)
rows.detail: THIS SECTION IS A VERBATIM REPRINT OF THE FY2012 REPORT'S TEXT and describes the 2011-2012 school year: 'a record 823 applications', '380 freshmen and 24 upperclassmen were admitted', VIP serving 'approximately 675 area students'.

The FY2013 Abstract of Assessments is the only one of the three years with a complete Accts column AND an account total in its TOTALS row (5,054), which also ties to the Accounts column of the valuation history. The other two years lost most of their counts.

The Sewers row of the long-term debt table is restated between the FY2012 and FY2013 reports — $3,323,639 for FY2012 here against $1,670,000 there, and similarly for every prior year — roughly doubling outside-the-limit debt while the grand total is unchanged. Something was reclassified and neither report says what.
STUDENT BUS FEES appears in the receipts for the first time at $31,916.83. A new charge on households shows up as a revenue line and nowhere else.
Building permit revenue has fallen by two thirds in three years: $181,516 (FY2011), $96,279 (FY2012), $61,956 (FY2013).

Grade 8 science at Lunenburg High School scored 34% advanced/proficient against a state average of 39% in the same year grade 10 science scored 97% and ranked 6th of 341 schools in the state. Both figures are on p41.

Special education Indicator 5 shows Lunenburg placing 77% of students with IEPs in full inclusion against a state rate of 58.1%, and only 4.5% in separate or residential settings against 6.8% — the placement mix is materially different from the state's, which bears directly on out-of-district cost.

Monty Tech's state and federal grants fell from $1,407,959 to $922,132 while private and competitive grants rose from $20,918 to $358,245, leaving the total nearly flat. A budget line barely moving while its funding source changes completely.

Article 27 rewrote the salary step ladder from an irregular 0/1/2/4/6/8/10/12-year schedule to annual advancement through step 3 and every two years thereafter, and the Finance Committee reported no additional financial impact. The dollar value of a step is printed nowhere in the report.
Three town offices were contested in 2013 (Selectmen, Town Clerk, School Committee) after two years in which nearly every race had one candidate and a Blanks row.

rows.table: Special education DESE indicator results, Lunenburg against state
rows.detail: Note the p34 narrative gives total enrollment as 1,587 where p32 and p33 give 1,602 — the two special services paragraphs are otherwise identical and one has a stale denominator.

rows.table: Monty Tech enrollment, admissions and Class of 2012 awards (reprinted from the FY2012 report)
rows.detail: The FY2013 report evidently carries two Monty Tech submissions, one current (pp44-57) and one stale (pp58-59), and there is no October 2013 enrollment-by-town breakdown anywhere in this document.

rows.table: Monty Tech MCAS results 2011-2013, by subject
rows.detail: The narrative gives 2013 passing rates as ELA 99%, Math 98%, Biology 97% but dates them 'spring of 2012', which contradicts the table.

rows.table: Board and committee regular meeting schedule
rows.detail: Differs from FY2012 in ways worth noting: an Assessors row appears, the Historical Commission moves from the Library to Ritter, PACC moves to Eagle House, the Sewer Commission and Cemetery Commission move to the DPW Office, the Zoning Board moves to Town Hall, and the Housing Partnership row disappears.

rows.detail: The FY2009 total is $29,490,706, agreeing with FY2012 and disagreeing with FY2011's $22,490,706.
